Name: Posets, complete lattices, monotone functions, adjoints
Paper Ref: Sec. 2 — "We assume familiarity with [...] order theory [39]"
Mathematical Concept: PartialOrder, CompleteLattice, GaloisConnection. Posetal adjoint functor theorem: F join-preserving ⟺ F has right adjoint.
Notes / Delta: Full infrastructure available including posetal AFT.

Name: Knaster-Tarski theorem (least and greatest fixed points)
Mathematical Concept: OrderHom.lfp, OrderHom.gfp. Fixed point induction: F(x)≤x ⟹ µF≤x. ω-continuous variant.
Notes / Delta: Both µF and νF available. ω-continuous induction in OmegaCompletePartialOrder.

Name: Basic category theory (functors, natural transformations, monads)
Paper Ref: Sec. 2 — "We assume familiarity with [...] basic category theory [96]"
Mathematical Concept: Functor, NatTrans, Monad (Haskell typeclass and categorical object).
Notes / Delta: Complete categorical infrastructure available.

Name: Initial algebras and free monads
Bibliographic Source: Goguen et al. 1977 [59] / Lamiaux & Ahrens 2024 [88] / Fiore, Plotkin & Turi 1999 [49] / Fiore 2008 [48]
Mathematical Concept: InitialAlgebra, FreeMonad generated by a signature functor Σ. Free monad S maps A to µx.A+Σx.
Notes / Delta: Monad available. InitialAlgebra as explicit object absent from Mathlib standard. Custom formalization required.

Name: Allegory
Mathematical Concept: Set A with: monoid multiplication ; (unit ∆), partial order ≤, meet ∧ making ; monotone, order-preserving contravariant involution −◦. Modular law: a;b∧c ≤ (a∧c;b◦);b.
Notes / Delta: Core typeclass to define from scratch. Coreflexives (a≤∆) simulate subsets / unary predicates. Reflexive: ∆≤a; transitive: a;a≤a; symmetric: a◦≤a.

Name: Locally-complete allegory (Relation Algebra / RA)
Mathematical Concept: Allegory with complete lattice such that ; and ∧ distribute over arbitrary joins. Gives: iteration a*=µx.∆∨a;x, right implication a→b (a;b≤c ⟺ b≤a→c), left implication b←a.
Notes / Delta: Paper calls this simply 'RA'. Division allegory residuals (a→b, b←a) needed for substitution adjunction ·[b]⊣b»·. Residuals absent from Mathlib at allegory level.

Name: Relator / colax relator / semirelator / ω-cocontinuous relator
Bibliographic Source: Kawahara 1973 [81] / Bird & de Moor 1997 [19] / Backhouse et al. 1991 [11] / Backhouse & Hoogendijk 1993 [12]
Mathematical Concept: Relator: monotone functor F:A→B preserving converse F(a◦)=(Fa)◦. Colax: F∆≤∆ and F(a;b)≤Fa;Fb. Semirelator: colax with F(a;b)=Fa;Fb (strict). ω-cocontinuous: preserves joins of ω-chains [8].
Notes / Delta: Four related notions as typeclass hierarchy. Semirelator most used downstream. ω-cocontinuity needed for TRA Condition 1. Allegories viewed as one-object categories (monoids).

Name: Cocartesian decomposition and cocartesian relator triple
Mathematical Concept: Pair of semirelators (Fl, Fr) such that F=Fl∨Fr and Fl;Fr≤⊥. Triple (F, Fl, Fr). Generalizes to n-ary.
Notes / Delta: Original Gavazzo construction. Captures coproduct structure V+Σ(−) of syntax at relational level. Directly used in TRA Def. 6 Condition 1 and Operational Decomposition Def. 23.

Name: Term Relation Algebra (TRA)
Mathematical Concept: RA A + cocartesian relator triple (ẽ·, ∆η, ·̂) + colax birelator ·[·] such that: (1) ẽ ω-cocontinuous; (2) aH = unique solution x=x̂;a with ∆H=∆; (3) closed monoid (A,∆η,·[·]) with ·[b]⊣b»·; (4) ã[b]≤ã[b].
Notes / Delta: CENTRAL DEFINITION. (1)=coproduct/initial algebra structure. (2)=initiality gives aH=Howe extension [73], structural induction [89]: x̂≤x⟹∆≤x. (3)=substitution monoid laws. (4)=syntax-preservation of substitution. First explicit axiomatization.

Name: Compatible, CUI, substitutive, Leibniz's law
Mathematical Concept: Compatible: a≤â. Closed under term constructs: a≤ã. CUI: a[∆]≤a. Substitutive: a[a]≤a. Leibniz: ∆[a]≤a. Compatible ⟹ reflexive (∆≤a). a[∆] always CUI.
Notes / Delta: Key predicates on relations used throughout. Note: compatibility implies Leibniz's law (converse generally false).

Name: Modalities □, ♦ and open extension ♢
Mathematical Concept: □a ≜ a[⊥] (closed/complete terms). ♦a ≜ a»⊥. Open extension: ♢a ≜ ∆»♦a. Laws: □∆η=⊥, (□a)[b]=□a, □(a;b)=□a;□b. □ is S4-comonad [20]. Adjoint cohesion: □⊣♦.
Notes / Delta: Novel structure revealed by TRAs. □ and ♦ form axiomatic cohesion [92]. Essential for closed reductions, big-step evaluation on closed terms, similarity, and open extension ♢ for congruence.

Name: Lemma 16: Closed monotone functions preserve closedness under fixed points
Mathematical Concept: F closed (□F(x)≤F(□x)) ⟹ □µF=µx.□F(x). In particular: □aF=(□a)F and □a⇓=(□a)⇓.
Notes / Delta: Technical lemma ensuring fixed-point constructions preserve completeness. Critical for Proposition 29 and Theorem 31 (if a closed then a⇓ closed).

Name: Harmony axiom
Mathematical Concept: For any compatible relation b: ⟨â,a⟩ ; b ≤ b ; a[b]. Computation is parametric: behaviour of b is fully determined by outermost operators and their sub-terms.
Notes / Delta: Additional axiom of the TRA framework beyond Definition 6, required by Lemma 34 (S3) and Theorem 35 (S4). Not derivable from the four TRA axioms alone. Must be declared explicitly in Lean 4 and verified on every concrete instantiation. Connected to proof-theoretic harmony [45][129] and Plotkin structural rules [122].

Name: Operational decomposition
Mathematical Concept: Decomposition of ẽ as cocartesian relator triple (·, ·, ⟨·,·⟩) for constructors vs destructors. Substitution distributes over both. □ distributes over ⟨·,b⟩. Value coreflexive: ∆κ ≜ □∆.
Notes / Delta: Algebraizes Martin-Löf [99] intro/elim form distinction. Captures CBN vs CBV uniformly. Constructors and destructors disjoint: ·;⟨b,c⟩≤⊥. CBN: no eval under intro forms. CBV: via reduced/fine-grain syntax [94][89].

Name: Gentzen's Inversion Principle (GIP)
Mathematical Concept: a ≤ ⟨∆⟩ ; a (i.e. a = ⟨∆⟩;a). Computation arises when elimination form has introduction form as major argument. Abbreviation ⟨a⟩ ≜ ⟨a,∆⟩.
Notes / Delta: LOCAL CONDITION 1 for bridge Theorem 37. Checkable by syntax inspection. Holds for β, βv and most standard reductions. Implies ∆η;a=⊥ for reductions. SGIP: dom(a)=⟨∆⟩ (stronger, requires typing).

Name: Gentzen's Conservation Principle (GCP)
Mathematical Concept: For any compatible x: ⟨x̂, x⟩ ; a ≤ a ; x[x]. Computation is parametric in subterms and proceeds by substitution.
Notes / Delta: LOCAL CONDITION 2 for bridge Theorem 37. Needed for congruence (Lemma 34) and confluence (Lemma 36). Connected to proof-theoretic harmony [45][129] and Plotkin structural rules [122]. Holds for β and βv. 'Embryonic version' due to Lassen [89].

Name: aF operator (structural recursion on elimination forms)
Mathematical Concept: aF = least solution of x = (∆ ∨ ⟨x⟩) ; a. Refines aH: operates on elimination forms (recursively evaluates major args) instead of all terms.
Notes / Delta: Intermediate operator between TRA structure and big-step evaluation. Least solution exists by Knaster-Tarski + ω-cocontinuity of ⟨·⟩. aE=(a∨∆)F is one-step evaluation.

Name: Reduction
Bibliographic Source: Bezem et al. 2003 [18] — Term Rewriting Systems
Mathematical Concept: Relation a such that ∆η ; a = ⊥. Variables are not reducible.
Notes / Delta: Standard nontriviality condition [18]. Ensures substitution instances only apply to non-variable terms. Holds for β and βv.

Name: Parallel reduction a⇛ and convertibility a≈
Bibliographic Source: Takahashi 1995 [141] / Howe 1996 [73] — via TRA abstraction by Gavazzo
Notes / Delta: Parallel reduction as Howe extension of reflexive substitution closure. Key insight from [53]: same algebraic construction as Howe's method. Standard TRA calculations show a≈=(a⇛∨a⇛◦)∗.

Name: Church-Rosser property, diamond property, confluence
Bibliographic Source: Church & Rosser 1936 [29] / Bezem et al. 2003 [18] / Struth [139][140]
Mathematical Concept: CR: (a∨a◦)∗=a∗;a∗◦. Diamond: a◦;a≤a;a◦. Confluent: a∗ has diamond property. CR ⟺ confluent [139][140].
Notes / Delta: Abstract confluence notions partially in Mathlib but not at TRA/RA level. CR↔confluent equivalence needs TRA-specific algebraic proof using [139][140].

Name: Orthogonality condition
Mathematical Concept: a[∆]◦;a[∆]≤∆ (deterministic substitution instances) AND a[∆]◦;ã[∆]⇛≤a◦[a⇛] (redex structure preserved under parallel sub-reduction).
Notes / Delta: Semantic orthogonality abstracting syntactic left-linearity and absence of critical pairs. Typically checkable by syntax inspection. Holds for β. Second condition is non-trivial; implies parallel moves.

Name: Theorem 21: Confluence of orthogonal reduction
Paper Ref: Thm. 21 — proved in [53], stated in this paper
Mathematical Concept: a orthogonal ⟹ a⇛ has diamond property ⟹ a⇛ confluent.
Notes / Delta: Proved algebraically in [53] using only TRA laws. Used as part (i) of bridge Theorem 37 via Lemma 36. No syntax-specific arguments needed.

Name: One-step evaluation aE
Mathematical Concept: aE ≜ (a ∨ ∆)F. Either relates intro forms with themselves or recursively evaluates major args of an elim form then a-reduces.
Notes / Delta: Bridge between reduction and big-step evaluation. Refines parallel reduction following CBN/CBV strategy of operational decomposition. □aE=(□a)E.

Name: Big-step evaluation a⇓
Mathematical Concept: a⇓ ≜ aE∗ ; ∆κ. Iterate aE until canonical form. □a⇓=(□a)⇓. If a closed then a⇓ closed.
Notes / Delta: Algebraic formulation of natural/big-step semantics covering CBN and CBV uniformly. The squeezing ;∆κ ensures output is a canonical form. Applies to CBV λ-calculus: □β⇓ coincides with standard ⇓βv.

Name: Proposition 29: Inductive characterization of a⇓
Mathematical Concept: a⇓ = least solution of x = ∆ ∨ ⟨x⟩ ; a ; x. If a closed: x = ∆κ ∨ ⟨x⟩ ; a ; x.
Notes / Delta: Connects algebraic definition to rule-based presentations of big-step semantics. Key intermediate result for Theorem 31 proof. Proof: show aE is least solution of x=∆∨⟨x⟩;a, then exploit least fixed point characterization of a∗.

Name: Theorem 31: Determinism of big-step evaluation
Mathematical Concept: a closed reduction, a;a◦≤∆ ⟹ a⇓◦;a⇓≤∆κ. Deterministic ground reduction ⟹ deterministic big-step evaluation.
Notes / Delta: NEW result. Proof: GIP ⟹ inversion lemma ⟨b⟩;a⇓≤⟨b;a⇓⟩;a⇓ ⟹ a◦;a⇓≤a⇓ ⟹ a⇓◦;a⇓≤∆κ. Corresponds to theorem (†) in Section 1.3 walkthrough. Part (ii) of bridge Theorem 37.

Name: b-simulation, similarity b⪆, bisimilarity b=∼
Mathematical Concept: B(a)=(b⪆;a)←b⪆. a is b-simulation if a≤B(♢a). b⪆=νx.B(♢x). Open similarity ♢b⪆=νx.♢B(x). Bisimilarity b=∼=νx.♢x∧B(♢x◦)◦.
Notes / Delta: Coinductive definitions requiring νF (greatest fixed points) in Lean 4. b⪆ is closed preorder: □∆≤b⪆, b⪆;b⪆≤b⪆, □b⪆=b⪆. Open similarity ♢b⪆ also a preorder. Both admit coinductive proof principles.

Name: op-Howe extension a§
Bibliographic Source: Howe 1996 [73] / Lassen 1998 [89] — dual construction by Gavazzo
Mathematical Concept: a§ ≜ (♢a)H◦. For any closed preorder a: ∆≤a§, a§[a§]≤a§, â§≤a§ (compatible), ♢a;a§≤a§ (quasi-transitivity).
Notes / Delta: 'Op-Howe' = dual of standard Howe extension applied to closed relations. Key instrument for Lemma 34. The four properties (§1)-(§4) proved as Lemma B.7 in the working draft appendix.

Name: Lemma 34: Key Lemma for congruence
Mathematical Concept: a closed reflexive transitive simulation + b satisfies GCP ⟹ a§ ≤ ♢B(a§). Proof by fixed point induction on b⪆. Long equational calculation using Harmony, GCP, and properties of a§.
Notes / Delta: Core technical lemma for congruence. Main content of Appendix B in working draft. Uses Harmony axiom: for compatible b, ⟨â,a⟩;b≤b;a[b]. Requires careful sequencing of GCP, §-properties, and structural laws.

Name: Theorem 35: Congruence of open similarity
Mathematical Concept: ♢b⪆ is substitutive and compatible. ♢b=∼ is a congruence.
Notes / Delta: NEW main result on semantic equivalence. Proof: Lemma 34 ⟹ b⪆§ open simulation ⟹ b⪆§≤♢b⪆ by coinduction. Since ♢b⪆≤b⪆§, conclude b⪆§=♢b⪆ and thus compatibility and substitutivity. Part (iii) of bridge Theorem 37.

Name: Lemma 36: GCP+GIP imply orthogonality condition
Mathematical Concept: a reduction satisfying GCP and GIP ⟹ a[∆]◦;ã[∆]⇛ ≤ a◦[a⇛]. Short proof using x;a⇛≤x̂;a⇛.
Notes / Delta: Bridge lemma connecting local conditions (GIP, GCP) to the orthogonality condition required by Theorem 21 (R5). Relatively short proof. Crucial link in the chain to confluence.

Name: Theorem 37: Bridge Theorem (MAIN RESULT)
Mathematical Concept: a[∆] deterministic + GIP + GCP ⟹ (i) a⇛ confluent [R5+M1]; (ii) (□a)⇓ deterministic [B4]; (iii) ♢((□a)=∼) congruence [S4].
Notes / Delta: MAIN RESULT. Three fundamental metatheorems from two local algebraic conditions. Once a term structure carries TRA and ground semantics satisfies GIP+GCP, all three conclusions are free. Unifies Aczel's confluence theorem [7] and Howe's congruence of bisimilarity [73] for second-order terms.

Name: First-order terms as TRA (Def. 8, Section 3.1.1)
Bibliographic Source: Goguen et al. 1977 [59] / Fiore, Plotkin & Turi 1999 [49]
Mathematical Concept: Given signature Σ and variables V, the dependent set TΣ(V) of terms in context carries a TRA. Variable coreflexive: x∆ηx. Strict compatible refinement: op(t̄) ẽ op(s̄) iff tᵢ ϕ sᵢ for all i. Substitution: t[τ] ϕ[ψ] s[σ] iff ∃Γ. t ϕ s and τ(x) ψ σ(x) for all x.
Notes / Delta: INSTANTIATION 1. Must verify all four TRA axioms (Def. 6) for first-order terms. (1) ẽ ω-cocontinuous: follows from finite signature. (2) Howe extension = relational initiality: follows from structural recursion. (3) Substitution monoid laws: standard equational theory of substitution. (4) Syntax-preservation: op(t̄)[σ]=op(t̄[σ]). Foundational example before lambda calculus.

Name: Lambda calculus (second-order terms) as TRA (Def. 10-12, Section 3.1.2)
Bibliographic Source: Fiore, Plotkin & Turi 1999 [49] / Aczel 1978 [7] / Gabbay & Pitts 1999 [52] / Pitts 2013 [115] / Lassen 1998 [89]
Mathematical Concept: Binding signature Σ = {lam:(1), app:(0,0)}. Terms TΣα(V) = TΣ(V)/∼α (modulo α-equivalence). Dependent relations on TΣα form a RA. TRA structure defined on raw terms then shown invariant under ∼α. Capture-avoiding substitution via structural or natural number recursion [116][15][138].
Notes / Delta: INSTANTIATION 2 (main instantiation of the thesis). Must verify TRA axioms for second-order terms with binders. Key challenge: capture-avoidance in substitution definition. Three approaches: nominal sets [52][115], Fiore-Plotkin-Turi presheaf method [49], or Stoughton's first-order encoding [138]. Must also show TRA structure is well-defined on ∼α-equivalence classes.

Name: Operational decomposition for λ-calculus (Examples 25-26)
Mathematical Concept: Σintro = {lam:(1)}. Σelim = {app:(0,0)} with app major position underlined. Correspondence: app ∼ lam. CBN: app(t,s) evaluates t until lam(x.t'), then reduces. CBV (Example 26): evaluate both t and s.
Notes / Delta: Must define operational decomposition (O1) explicitly for the λ-calculus TRA. Define relational operators · and ⟨·,·⟩ induced by the intro/elim split. Verify the three conditions of Def. 23: substitution distributes over both, □ distributes over ⟨·,b⟩. ∆κ=□∆ identifies closed λ-abstractions as canonical forms.

Name: β-reduction is a reduction satisfying GIP
Mathematical Concept: β: Γ,x ⊢ (λx.t)s β t[s/x]. Verify: (1) ∆η;β=⊥ (variables not reducible). (2) GIP: β ≤ ⟨∆⟩;β — i.e. β only fires on app(lam(−),−), an elimination form with introduction form as major argument.
Notes / Delta: Verification of LOCAL CONDITION 1 (O2) for β. Both conditions are straightforward by inspection of the β-rule definition. ∆η;β=⊥ because (λx.t)s is not a variable. GIP holds because app ∈ Σelim and lam ∈ Σintro with app∼lam.

Name: β[∆] is deterministic (a[∆]◦;a[∆]≤∆)
Mathematical Concept: β[∆]◦;β[∆]≤∆: substitution instances of β-reduction are deterministic. Explicitly: if (λx.t)s β t[s/x] and (λx.t)s β t'[s'/x] then t[s/x]=t'[s'/x].
Notes / Delta: First condition of orthogonality (R4) for β. Follows immediately from the deterministic shape of the β-rule: the redex (λx.t)s uniquely determines the reduct t[s/x]. Standard result, algebraically expressible as a[∆]◦;a[∆]≤∆.

Name: β-reduction satisfies GCP
Mathematical Concept: For any compatible x: ⟨x̂,x⟩;β ≤ β;x[x]. Verified: if (λx.p)w ⟨ϕ,b ϕ⟩ (λx.u)v with w ϕ v and x⊢p ϕ u, then p[w/x] ϕ[ϕ] u[v/x], and (λx.p)w β p[w/x] gives the required inequality.
Notes / Delta: Verification of LOCAL CONDITION 2 (O3) for β. The paper gives this calculation explicitly in Section 6.1.1. Requires the Harmony axiom (H1) to hold for β. Key step: ⟨ϕ,b ϕ⟩;βv ≤ βv;ϕ[ϕ] for CBV. Must also verify H1 holds for β on the instantiation I2.

Name: Corollary: Bridge Theorem instantiated on λ-calculus
Mathematical Concept: β[∆] deterministic (I5) + β satisfies GIP (I4) + β satisfies GCP (I6) ⟹ (i) β⇛ confluent (Church-Rosser); (ii) (□β)⇓ deterministic (evaluation is deterministic); (iii) ♢((□β)=∼) is a congruence (applicative bisimilarity is a congruence).
Notes / Delta: FINAL RESULT of the instantiation chain. All three conclusions follow by M2 applied to I2-I6. This is the concrete payoff: Church-Rosser, determinism of CBN/CBV evaluation, and congruence of applicative bisimilarity for the λ-calculus all follow from two easily-checked local conditions. Zero additional proof needed beyond the abstract framework.
